content.study:
Topic at a Glance
Article 227 of the Constitution of India is titled “Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court”. It forms an integral component of The States (Articles 152–237), located within the “The States” cluster. Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023.

Constitutional Text & Anatomy
(1) Every High Court shall have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.

(5) and (6) . and further subs. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 31, for cl. (1) .

(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, the High Court may—

(a) call for returns from such courts;

(b) make and issue general rules and prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts; and

(c) prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts.

(3) The High Court may also settle tables of fees to be allowed to the sheriff and all clerks and officers of such courts and to attorneys, advocates and pleaders practising therein:

Provided that any rules made, forms prescribed or tables settled under clause (2) or clause (3) shall not be inconsistent with the provision of any law for the time being in force, and shall require the previous approval of the Governor.

(4) Nothing in this article shall be deemed to confer on a High Court powers of superintendence over any court or tribunal constituted by or under any law relating to the Armed Forces. 1(5) [omitted [omitted [omitted [omitted

Constituent Assembly Intent & Doctrinal Foundation
The framers envisioned Article 227 as a fundamental structural instrument. In constitutional jurisprudence, every clause operates not in isolation but as part of an integrated, transformative organic document. It regulates executive, legislative, or fundamental citizen interests to maintain the rule of law and constitutional supremacy.

Procedural & Courtroom Anchors (Senior Counsel Checklist)
1. Competent Forum: Extraordinary original constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32). High Court jurisdiction extends to Fundamental Rights and “for any other purpose”.
2. Standard of Review: Judicial review of administrative, quasi-judicial, and legislative action on grounds of illegality, irrationality, procedural impropriety, or manifest arbitrariness.
3. Standing & Remedial Path: Aggrieved person for personal prerogative relief; expanded standing / PIL for public duty enforcement and marginalized groups.
4. Evidentiary Standards: Where disputed facts or legislative arbitrariness are alleged, evidentiary burdens under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA ss. 104–106) and official gazette notifications govern the record.

Key Statutory Ingredients to Establish
1. (1) Every High Court shall have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.
2. (5) and (6) . and further subs. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 31, for cl. (1) .
3. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, the High Court may—
4. (a) call for returns from such courts;
5. (b) make and issue general rules and prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts; and
6. (c) prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts.

Judicial Interpretation & Binding Ratios
1. Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) (1973) 4 SCC 225: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land; constitutional provisions must be harmoniously construed to preserve its basic structure and core institutional balance.
2. Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980) (1980) 3 SCC 625: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles form the bedrock of the Constitution; institutional boundaries and constitutional discipline cannot be breached.

Current-Law Position & Milestone
Current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023. Any attempt by subordinate legislation or executive notifications to abridge the mandate of Article 227 is subject to judicial review under Articles 226 and 32.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Direct Application (Constitutional Guarantee / Power Upheld)
examples.body: State action or statutory exercise strictly satisfies the conditions laid down under Article 227 (Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court). The authority acts within constitutional bounds, respects procedural fairness, and advances the constitutional objective of The States. Outcome: Action is held valid and enforceable by the Court.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Condition / Breach (State Action Fails)
examples.body: An executive order or legislation violates or bypasses the express procedural conditions, jurisdictional threshold, or fundamental guarantees of Article 227. The action is tainted by manifest arbitrariness, lacks legislative competence, or ignores mandatory safeguards. Outcome: The Court strikes down the measure or issues a writ of certiorari / mandamus.

hypotheticals.question: Examine the constitutional validity of the impugned directive in light of Article 227 and settled Supreme Court jurisprudence. What relief, if any, can be granted?
hypotheticals.analysis:
1. Scrutinize the constitutional source of power: Does Article 227 grant plenary power, or is it conditioned by express safeguards, legislative competence, or fundamental rights?
2. Apply the doctrine of ultra vires and manifest arbitrariness: If the directive creates arbitrary exceptions or bypasses statutory provisions, it violates Article 14 and the mandate of Article 227.
3. Examine procedural compliance: Substantive and procedural requirements under the Constitution cannot be waived on mere grounds of administrative convenience.
4. Balance public interest vs constitutional discipline: Constitutional limitations always prevail over executive fiat.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Case Brief & Legal Assessment: Scope and Application of Article 227 (Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. ISSUE & CONSTITUTIONAL CONTEXT
Whether the State action, statutory enactment, or individual claim conforms to the constitutional mandate, procedural prerequisites, and substantive protections enshrined in Article 227 (Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court) of the Constitution of India.

II. RULE & STATUTORY ANATOMY
Article 227 is situated in The States (Articles 152–237), governing the “The States” dimension of Indian constitutional law.
The essential constitutional ingredients are:
1. (1) Every High Court shall have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.
2. (5) and (6) . and further subs. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 31, for cl. (1) .
3. (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, the High Court may—
4. (a) call for returns from such courts;
5. (b) make and issue general rules and prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts; and
6. (c) prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts.

III. PROCEDURAL ANCHOR & REMEDIAL FORUM
1. Competent Forum: Extraordinary original constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32). High Court jurisdiction extends to Fundamental Rights and “for any other purpose”.
2. Standard of Review: Judicial review of administrative, quasi-judicial, and legislative action on grounds of illegality, irrationality, procedural impropriety, or manifest arbitrariness.
3. Standing: Aggrieved person for personal prerogative relief; expanded standing / PIL for public duty enforcement and marginalized groups.

IV. JUDICIAL INTERPRETATION & AUTHORITY
In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) (1973) 4 SCC 225, the Supreme Court established that The Constitution is the supreme law of the land; constitutional provisions must be harmoniously construed to preserve its basic structure and core institutional balance.
Furthermore, in Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980) (1980) 3 SCC 625, the Court reaffirmed that constitutional guarantees are justiciable and binding upon all state functionaries.

V. APPLICATION TO FACT PATTERNS
To apply Article 227:
1. Verify whether the impugned measure falls within the scope of the article's textual command.
2. Check whether any express exceptions, provisos, or constitutional limitations apply.
3. Subject the measure to tests of proportionality and non-arbitrariness under Article 14. If an ingredient is missing or breached, the measure is unconstitutional.

VI. CONCLUSION
Article 227 stands as a vital constitutional checkpoint. Any state action in breach thereof is void and amenable to writ jurisdiction under Articles 32 and 226. Current through the 106th Amendment (2023).

questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. INTRODUCTION & CONSTITUTIONAL PHILOSOPHY
Article 227 of the Constitution of India, titled “Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court”, represents a critical cornerstone of India’s constitutional democracy. Situated within The States (Articles 152–237), the provision balances state power with individual liberties and institutional accountability. The Constituent Assembly intended this provision to be an active, living guarantee rather than an ornamental declaration.
II. STATUTORY & DOCTRINAL DECONSTRUCTION
A forensic analysis of Article 227 reveals the following distinct constitutional limbs:
(a) Limb 1: (1) Every High Court shall have superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction.
(a) Limb 2: (5) and (6) . and further subs. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 31, for cl. (1) .
(a) Limb 3: (2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, the High Court may—
(a) Limb 4: (a) call for returns from such courts;
(a) Limb 5: (b) make and issue general rules and prescribe forms for regulating the practice and proceedings of such courts; and
(a) Limb 6: (c) prescribe forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by the officers of any such courts.
The Article must be read in conjunction with the foundational architecture of the Constitution:
1. Separation of Powers & Checks and Balances: No branch of government possesses untrammelled discretion.
2. Rule of Law & Non-Arbitrariness: Every exercise of authority under Article 227 must satisfy the basic standard of fairness and reasonableness.
3. Transformative Constitutionalism: The provision must be interpreted progressively to advance justice, liberty, and equality as pledged in the Preamble.
III. JURISPRUDENTIAL EVOLUTION & LEADING CASE LAW
The Supreme Court of India has deconstructed Article 227 across several seminal judgments:
1. Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) (1973) 4 SCC 225:
   Ratio Decidendi: The Constitution is the supreme law of the land; constitutional provisions must be harmoniously construed to preserve its basic structure and core institutional balance.
2. Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980) (1980) 3 SCC 625:
   Ratio Decidendi: Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles form the bedrock of the Constitution; institutional boundaries and constitutional discipline cannot be breached.
IV. PROCEDURAL ROADMAP & LITIGATION CHECKLIST (SENIOR COUNSEL REFERENCE)
When approaching the Court under or in respect of Article 227:
1. Forum Selection: Extraordinary original constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court (Art. 226) or Supreme Court (Art. 32). High Court jurisdiction extends to Fundamental Rights and “for any other purpose”.
2. Pleading Essentials: The writ petition or plaint must specifically plead:
   (a) The exact constitutional authority or violation under Article 227;
   (b) The factual narrative establishing how each statutory ingredient is satisfied or infringed;
   (c) The absence of an effective alternative remedy, or justification under the Whirlpool Corporation exceptions (breach of fundamental rights, violation of natural justice, or complete lack of jurisdiction).
3. Evidentiary Standard: Discharge of burden under BSA ss. 104–106 and production of certified records.
V. IRAC PROBLEM ANALYSIS (PRACTICE HYPOTHETICAL)
Fact Matrix: The State issues a notification encroaching upon the domain of Article 227 without satisfying statutory preconditions.
Issue: Does the executive notification violate the constitutional guarantees and procedures of Article 227?
Rule: Under Article 227, state action is strictly conditioned by constitutional provisions and cannot be exercised arbitrarily.
Application: The impugned notification fails because it circumvents the procedural safeguards and lacks rational nexus to the constitutional objective. Applying the proportionality test, the State has failed to adopt the least intrusive means.
Conclusion: The notification is unconstitutional and void ab initio. The appropriate writ of certiorari or mandamus shall issue.
VI. CRITICAL APPRAISAL & CURRENT-LAW MILESTONE
Article 227 remains a vibrant instrument of governance, current through the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023. A robust democracy requires rigorous adherence to its letter and spirit to protect the citizen against executive overreach and legislative excesses.
